ftm.office_official: Register of Wills for Baltimore County - Alexis Burrell-Rohde, Register of Wills for Baltimore County
ftm.office_address: County Courts Building, 401 Bosley Avenue, Room 500, Towson, Maryland 21204
ftm.notes: The office encourages calling before visiting to ensure all required documents are prepared. Online estate search is available statewide via https://registers.maryland.gov/main/search.html. Filings cannot be accepted via email. Original wills can be mailed for safekeeping with a $5 fee. Drop box available for submissions, with last pickup at 3:30 p.m. Copies can be requested online or by phone.

ftm.office_official: Circuit Court for Baltimore County, Clerk's Office
ftm.notes: The online Daily Docket includes all scheduled events for Civil, Criminal, and Domestic cases, updated between 4 and 4:30 p.m. each day for the next day's docket. Foreclosure complaints (judicial foreclosures) would appear here. For nonjudicial foreclosures, check the Recorder/Register of Deeds for Notice of Trustee Sale filings. Information is subject to change; verify courtroom assignments on monitors at the courthouse. No direct search for 'foreclosure' on the daily docket, requires manual review of civil cases.

ftm.data_type: Recorder / Register of Deeds - Lien & Deed Index
ftm.office_official: Clerk of the Circuit Court, Land Records Division
ftm.phone: 410-887-2650 (Baltimore County Land Records), 410-887-3088 (Circuit Court Land Records Office)
ftm.notes: Maryland Land Records (MDLandRec) is the digital repository for land records, including deeds, mortgages, and various liens (mechanic's, IRS & state tax, HOA, child-support, lis pendens). Requires account creation for full access. Tax and child-support liens are indexed against the person, requiring name-matching to the assessor roll. The site provides a search guide and contact for helpdesk.

ftm.office_official: Office of Budget and Finance, Taxpayer Services
ftm.phone: 410-887-5616 (Tax Sale Information), 410-887-3313 (Office of Budget and Finance)
ftm.updates: Annually (list updated weekly prior to sale)
ftm.notes: Baltimore County conducts an annual tax sale for properties with unpaid real property taxes. The notice of advertisement is published weekly for four weeks prior to the sale. The list is updated on Thursdays. Property owners have six months from the sale date to redeem the property. Penalties and fees apply to delinquent accounts. Past winning bidder reports are available on the website.

ftm.office_official: Office of Budget and Finance, Taxpayer Services
ftm.notes: Delinquent notices are mailed in February to all taxpayers with unpaid accounts. Any unpaid balances past December 31 are considered delinquent and subject to interest and penalties. The full pre-sale roll is not directly published online as a single list, but the tax sale list serves as the pre-auction delinquent roll. Individual property tax payment status can be checked via the PropertyTaxPayment system (mytax.baltimorecountymd.gov).

ftm.office_official: N/A (Baltimore County handles county-wide property taxes)
ftm.notes: Baltimore County handles property taxes for the entire county, including incorporated areas. There is no separate 'city tax delinquency' list for individual incorporated cities within Baltimore County. Baltimore City (a separate jurisdiction) has its own tax sale and delinquency process.

ftm.office_official: Department of Permits, Approvals and Inspections (PAI), Code Enforcement Division
ftm.notes: PAI handles code enforcement for all of Baltimore County. The website provides information on how to report a violation and common violations. An online portal for searching specific code violations by address is not readily apparent from the main page, suggesting a records request or direct inquiry may be needed for detailed lists. They use an online complaint form for reporting.

ftm.office_official: N/A (Baltimore County handles code enforcement for all areas)
ftm.notes: Baltimore County's Department of Permits, Approvals and Inspections (PAI) handles code enforcement for all areas within Baltimore County, including incorporated towns. There is no separate city-level code violation system for individual incorporated cities within the county.

ftm.office_official: Department of Permits, Approvals and Inspections (PAI), Code Enforcement Division
ftm.notes: Information regarding condemned, unsafe structures, or demolition orders would fall under the purview of Code Enforcement. While the website details general code enforcement, a specific public list or database for condemned/unsafe structures is not explicitly provided. A public records request or direct contact with the department would likely be necessary to obtain such a list.

ftm.office_official: District Court of Maryland for Baltimore County, Clerk's Office
ftm.office_address: 120 E. Chesapeake Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204 (Towson District Court)
ftm.notes: Eviction (failure to pay rent, tenant holding over) cases are heard in the District Court. To identify 'multiple-eviction landlords,' one would need to access the court's electronic docket (Maryland Judiciary Case Search) and search by plaintiff name. This requires knowing landlord names or performing broad searches and filtering. The public portal does not easily allow for bulk data extraction or searching for patterns like multiple filings by a single entity.

ftm_narrative: Data gaps to know about: SiftMap data (provider data) is low or zero in Baltimore County, MD for: Foreclosure notices, Tax sale list. These are proven deal-makers nationally, and nobody can buy them here, so the county pulls below are not a backup, they are the only way in: treat them as priority pulls. Also not in SiftMap here: Eviction filings, Code violations, Divorce filings.
Sources pulled straight from the county the day records publish, 30 to 90 days before paid data. 'Verify locally' means confirm the link before you work it.

read_me.Doors/deal: Live list size divided by the deals that list produced in the window. Lower is better: fewer doors to work per closed deal.
read_me.Lift: County baseline doors/deal divided by the signal's doors/deal. 3.0 means three times sharper than pulling the whole county.
read_me.Baseline: The whole county unfiltered, counted the same way; the denominator every signal is judged against.
read_me.Stack: Records sitting on two distress lists at once. Stacks are distress plus distress; AI is never AND-stacked on distress.
read_me.AI score: DataSift Investor AI likelihood-to-sell score, 0-100, a PARALLEL pull alongside the distress lists.
read_me.score-gated: Live AI-scored supply counts are provisioned per account, so a local doors/deal cannot be computed in this view. The deals and coverage are this county's own data.
read_me.Verify supply: The row tripped the verify rule (v2.1 coverage-aware: verify reasons annotate (churn: doors/deal < 5; small: list < 250) without demoting; only judicial notice lists and churn artifacts (doors/deal < 1) force P3. Volume floors: P1 needs >=2% of county deal flow or >=25 deals, P2 >=1% or >=12 deals): demand is real, treat the efficiency as directional until you price the live list.
read_me.Evidence A / B / C: from this county's own sold deals / cross-market benchmark / single-market anchor (Knox + Blount TN AI measurement)
read_me.Typical gross: Median of AVM value minus purchase price on clean deals: acquisition spread, not net profit.
read_me.Non-disclosure states: Sale prices are not public there, so deal-dollar columns are omitted; doors/deal and lift never use dollars.
